title: Roha fatality inquiry put on hold
article: An inquiry into the death of Tamer Sayed Roha will continue at a later date after the presiding judge indicated a need for more witnesses.
Provincial court Judge Anne Brown said calling more witnesses would provide greater insight into Roha's past, which includes several hospitalizations for cocaine-induced psychosis.
"I think we need to look at things that happened earlier," Brown told the family of Roha on Wednesday.
The inquiry will reconvene Oct. 23 to set a date to hear more testimony.
Roha, 27, died Sept. 4, 2002, shortly after police handcuffed him in his room at the Quality Inn on Banff Trail N.W.
Officers who attended the scene had received reports of a man acting oddly and disturbing other guests. Eight days before his death, Roha was hospitalized under similar circumstances.
The inquiry, originally scheduled for two days, includes representatives from the attorney general's office, the Calgary Police Service, City of Calgary and the Calgary Health Region.
